protocol.supervision_model: Not stated using 'collaborative'/'autonomous' prescribing terminology in the extracted text. The protocol requires that when modifying pharmacotherapy within the Program that has been prescribed by another healthcare provider, changes are attempted in collaboration with the original prescriber or the patient's usual healthcare provider (whichever is most appropriate), and that a copy of the patient's COPD Action Plan is provided to their usual healthcare provider and other relevant healthcare professionals involved in the patient's respiratory care (L: Collaborative care).
protocol.scope_summary: Queensland Community Pharmacy Chronic Conditions Management Pilot clinical protocol for the Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Monitoring Program. Eligibility is assessed at each consultation (patient must not meet any ineligibility criterion; the visible list starts with age <35 years, pregnancy, respiratory distress, exercise-related chest tightness without other COPD symptoms, and features of a respiratory condition other than COPD). Patients with symptoms and features of mild COPD and asthma (including co-existing asthma and COPD) are managed under the Improved Asthma Symptom Control Program protocol after confirming COPD Monitoring Program eligibility. Readable content covers non-pharmacological measures and optimising function (smoking/vaping cessation, immunisation, physical activity, pulmonary rehabilitation referral, diet/nutrition, weight management, lung cancer screening referral), pharmacotherapy for stable mild COPD as a three-step stepwise pathway per Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory (Step 1 short-acting bronchodilator therapy; Step 2 long-acting bronchodilator monotherapy; Step 3 long-acting bronchodilator dual therapy), inhaler considerations, management and treatment of COPD exacerbations (including an up-to-5-day prednis(ol)one self-initiation prescription with no repeats and antibiotic-restriction/referral rules), confirmation and communication of the management plan, collaborative care, and the start of clinical review and ongoing collaboration. NOTE: the text extraction is materially incomplete and glyph-corrupted - only 7 extraction pages were produced from a document whose footers show 'Page 14 of 27' etc., so large parts of the protocol (sections A-H, continuation of the ineligibility list, most of section M, appendices and reference list) are absent (see open_questions). Ineligibility for treatment as part of a Pilot service does not preclude a patient from accessing services provided as part of usual pharmacy care.

diagnosis_pathways.name: Program eligibility assessment and referral (assessed at each consultation)

steps.description: Eligibility for the Program. Eligibility for participation in the Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Program must be assessed at each consultation, as eligibility may change due to changes in health status or demographic factors (i.e. patients who were previously eligible may become ineligible and patients who were ineligible may become eligible). Confirm the patient does not meet any ineligibility criterion. The visible ineligibility criteria are: are aged <35 years; are planning a pregnancy or are pregnant; are experiencing respiratory distress (e.g., unable to complete a whole sentence in one breath); during/after exercise experience chest tightness or discomfort (without other symptoms of COPD) - consider possibility of a cardiovascular condition/event; have clinical features, symptoms or findings suggestive of a respiratory condition other than COPD that is not suitable for management under the Program. The ineligibility list continues into content that is not present in this text extraction (see OQ-1). Manage patients with symptoms and features of mild COPD and asthma (including those with a diagnosis of co-existing asthma and COPD) under the clinical protocol for the Improved Asthma Symptom Control Program; confirm that the patient meets the eligibility criteria of the COPD Monitoring Program before commencing treatment.

gates.criterion: Eligibility confirmed at this consultation and no ineligibility criterion is met (full ineligibility list must be applied - see OQ-1)

steps.description: Refer the patient to their usual healthcare provider (or emergency services, if required) with a comprehensive clinical handover if the patient is, or becomes, ineligible for management under the Program. Ineligibility for treatment as part of a Pilot service does not preclude a patient from accessing services provided as part of usual pharmacy care.

gates.criterion: Patient remains eligible for the Program and wishes to continue

steps.description: Smoking and vaping cessation, and immunisation. Detailed guidance for pharmacists supporting smoking cessation is contained in the Smoking Cessation Clinical Practice Guideline and supporting vaping cessation is contained in the E-cigarette and Vaping Cessation Guide. Immunisation: consider the immunisation status of patients with COPD, including for pneumococcal disease, RSV, COVID-19, influenza, pertussis and herpes zoster. Provide advice regarding the appropriateness based on the individual clinical circumstances, individual vaccine information provided by the TGA, current Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation (ATAGI) advice and the current version of the Australian Immunisation Handbook (partially glyph-corrupted in the extraction).

Optimising function - physical activity and referral for pulmonary rehabilitation. Many patients with COPD have a sedentary lifestyle and find physical activity difficult (part of this sentence is glyph-corrupted in the extraction); physical activity can improve exercise capacity and quality of life and reduce hospitalisations and improve quality of life. Encourage patients with COPD to undertake physical activity in line with recommendations for their age group in the Physical activity and exercise guidelines for all Australians; doing any amount of physical activity is better than none and patients should be encouraged to gradually build up to the recommendations. Encourage patients experiencing difficulty with physical activity to see a physiotherapist or exercise physiologist. Referral for pulmonary rehabilitation: pulmonary rehabilitation improves exercise capacity, mental health and quality of life regardless of COPD severity and can reduce the frequency of hospitalisations for exacerbations; encourage patients with COPD to participate in a pulmonary rehabilitation program when symptomatic and after an exacerbation; information about pulmonary rehabilitation programs (and other services including psychosocial support) available throughout Queensland, including how referrals can be made, can be found on the Lung Foundation Australia - Find a Service website.

Diet and nutrition, weight management, and referral for lung cancer screening. Malnutrition, obesity and poor nutritional status, generally resulting from suboptimal eating habits, sedentary lifestyle, smoking and corticosteroid use is common in patients with COPD, and has been shown to contribute to morbidity and mortality. Advice should focus on a balanced diet with foods from each of the 5 food groups in appropriate portions to maintain a healthy weight, in accordance with the Australian Dietary Guidelines. Weight management: encourage underweight and overweight patients to see a dietitian for tailored nutritional advice; detailed guidance for pharmacists supporting weight management is contained in the Management of Overweight and Obesity Clinical Practice Guideline. Referral for lung cancer screening: the screening criteria and program name are glyph-corrupted in the extraction (see OQ-2); eligible patients are referred using the National Lung Cancer Screening Program information for healthcare providers.

diagnosis_pathways.name: Pharmacotherapy for stable COPD, inhaler management, plan confirmation and communication

steps.description: I: Pharmacotherapy - stepwise pharmacotherapy for stable COPD. As COPD progresses, management using non-pharmacological measures alone may become inadequate and pharmacotherapy may be required to relieve symptoms, reduce the frequency of exacerbations and improve overall quality of life. Where pharmacotherapy is prescribed, the patient's prescription(s) (including repeats) should provide enough medicine for the period until the patient's next scheduled review. Patients entering the program with an existing medicine regimen: ask for the patient's most recent COPD Action Plan (if they have one) and consider whether the most recently prescribed pharmacotherapy is appropriate for the patient's symptoms and medical history, and optimised for the patient including inhaler technique and adherence. When modifying pharmacotherapy within the Program that has been prescribed by another healthcare provider, attempt to make changes in collaboration with the original prescriber or the patient's usual healthcare provider (whichever is most appropriate). Pharmacists may modify or deprescribe pharmacotherapy, particularly if the patient's response is inadequate (within appropriate clinical timeframes), the patient is experiencing intolerable/unmanageable adverse effects, the patient is unable to use the prescribed device correctly after appropriate training, or modification is clinically warranted and safe to do so; consider if the medicine is also used for another condition (e.g. maintenance oral corticosteroids for another condition). Pharmacotherapy for stable mild COPD within the Program must be in accordance with the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory (Stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) - Stepwise management of stable COPD), specifically: Step 1: Short-acting bronchodilator therapy; Step 2: Long-acting bronchodilator monotherapy; Step 3: Long-acting bronchodilator dual therapy. Combination products can be prescribed if appropriate, however they must only include medicines able to be prescribed under the Program.

gates.criterion: Pharmacotherapy sits within Step 1 to Step 3 of the Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory stepwise management of stable COPD, and includes only medicines able to be prescribed under the Program

steps.description: Key considerations for the stepwise pathway. The entry point to the stepwise pathway should be individualised to the patient's previous medical and medication history. Patients with a new diagnosis of COPD or managing COPD with non-pharmacological measures should generally initiate pharmacotherapy at Step 1. When commencing any medicine, patients should be advised to return if they experience adverse effects, an increase in symptom frequency or type, more severe symptoms or an exacerbation. Refer patients initiated on Step 3 Long-acting bronchodilator dual therapy (i.e. LAMA + LABA) where the condition has not stabilised or has worsened after 1 month to an appropriate healthcare provider for ongoing management.

gates.criterion: Condition has stabilised within 1 month of initiating Step 3 long-acting bronchodilator dual therapy (LAMA + LABA)

steps.description: Inhaler considerations. The choice of medicine and device should consider patient preference and their ability to use the device correctly with appropriate training, considering factors such as the inspiratory effort required, patient age, inspiratory effort capability, developmental stage, cognition and dexterity, and the environmental impact of the device (when in use and when disposed of). Recommend use of a spacer for people using pressured metered dose inhalers (with a face mask if required) to reduce issues with coordination, maximise lung deposition and reduce adverse effects of some medicines. Minimise the number of inhalers prescribed, and the different types of inhaler devices, where possible to avoid confusion; if the use of more than one inhaler device type is unavoidable, provide clear instructions for correct device use and handling and any differences (inspiratory effort required, shaking, storage, cleaning, disposal). Demonstrate the correct use of the patient's prescribed device (which may differ between brands) using a placebo inhaler and provide an inhaler-specific checklist. Review inhaler technique and adherence at every opportunity, even if the same inhaler or inhaler device has been used long-term. Further resources: National Asthma Council of Australia Inhaler technique for people with asthma or COPD, and Lung Foundation inhaler technique checklist (device specific checklists).

J: Confirm management plan is appropriate. Consult the Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory and the Australian Medicines Handbook and other relevant references to confirm that management is appropriate, including for: suitability of inhaler device; contraindications and precautions; drug interactions; lactation status.

gates.criterion: Management confirmed appropriate for inhaler device suitability, contraindications and precautions, drug interactions, and lactation status

provenance.section_heading: J: Confirm management plan is appropriate

steps.description: K: Communicate agreed management plan. Provide comprehensive advice (including supporting written information when required) to the patient regarding: individual product and medicine use (e.g., dosing and inhaler technique); how to manage adverse effects; non-pharmacological measures; how to self-manage their COPD (see Develop and implement a management plan); when to seek further care and/or treatment; when to return for clinical review. It is the pharmacist's responsibility to ensure the suitability and accuracy of any resources provided to patients (and/or caregivers if applicable), and compliance with all copyright conditions.

L: Collaborative care. Provide a copy of the patient's COPD Action Plan to their usual healthcare provider (and any other relevant healthcare professionals involved in the patient's respiratory care). The communication should also include (if appropriate): relevant medical history, results of any spirometry testing conducted and level of symptom control (CAAT score); changes to existing pharmacotherapy prescribed for COPD or new pharmacotherapy (including for exacerbations); a summary of advice provided to the patient including recommendations for multidisciplinary care and referrals; the next scheduled review appointment.

diagnosis_pathways.name: Recognition, self-management and review of COPD exacerbations, and ongoing clinical review

steps.description: Management and treatment of COPD exacerbations. Advise all patients on how to recognise an exacerbation, including the signs and symptoms that indicate the need for emergency medical care, and to commence treatment at the onset of symptoms; this should be included in the patient's COPD Action Plan. The source title immediately before 'Chapter 4: Management of exacerbations' is glyph-corrupted in the extraction, but the guidance has information to support pharmacists in assessing the severity of an exacerbation and differentiating conditions that may mimic or worsen exacerbation-like symptoms i.e., heart failure, pulmonary embolism.

provenance.section_heading: Management and treatment of COPD exacerbations

steps.description: Patient self-management of symptoms consistent with mild and moderate exacerbations, as per the Therapeutic Guidelines: Treatment of a COPD exacerbation. Instruct patients to use their bronchodilator as often as needed, clearly detailing the maximum dose that can be taken at one time and the maximum dose that can be taken in one 24-hour period (numeric values not printed in this document); ipratropium is contraindicated in patients taking a LAMA and has a slower onset of effect than salbutamol. Provide and dispense a prescription for up to 5 days treatment of prednis(ol)one with no repeats as part of the patient's written COPD Action Plan to self-initiate if symptoms persist or recur within four hours after reliever use. Instruct patients that they must arrange medical practitioner review as soon as possible after starting prednis(ol)one for the management of worsening COPD symptoms. Antibiotic therapy is only required when an exacerbation is triggered by a bacterial infection; refer a patient suspected of having a bacterial infection to an appropriate healthcare provider. Signs suggestive of bacterial infection or pneumonia include increased sputum volume, increased purulence and a possible change in colour, abnormally rapid breathing while at rest, fever and other infection signs (partly glyph-corrupted in the extraction); sputum colour (green) alone is not a reliable indicator of bacterial infection and needs to be interpreted in the context of the other signs and symptoms; sputum culture is not routinely recommended for COPD exacerbations. Advise all patients to return to the pharmacist (or their chosen healthcare provider) for review of their COPD Action Plan after an exacerbation, even if it was mild and self-managed.

gates.criterion: Exacerbation is consistent with mild or moderate symptoms suitable for self-management under the written COPD Action Plan
No signs suggestive of bacterial infection or pneumonia (otherwise refer to an appropriate healthcare provider)

provenance.section_heading: Patient self-management of symptoms consistent with mild and moderate exacerbations

steps.description: Advise patients to seek emergency care/call an ambulance (even if they have self-initiated prednis(ol)one) if: they have severe breathing difficulties; they have chest pain, 'fluttering' in the chest or an abnormally slow or racing heartbeat (arrythmia) (COPD exacerbations may present similarly to cardiovascular disease); they cannot manage or function at home e.g., can't walk between rooms, eat or sleep due to breathlessness; they cannot tolerate oral prednis(ol)one; they have drowsiness or confusion that may indicate hypercapnia or risk of hypercapnia; they notice the onset or worsening of central cyanosis; the oxygen saturation reading stated in the protocol (glyph-corrupted in the extraction, see OQ-3); they have leg swelling (peripheral oedema); they notice fluctuating blood pressure; bacterial infection or pneumonia is suspected; symptoms remain uncontrolled despite treatment with an inhaled bronchodilator and prednis(ol)one.

gates.criterion: None of the 'seek emergency care/call an ambulance' criteria are present
